milestones.claim: Stock-layout modified boot image executes an on-panel probe; RAM fastboot boot is not implemented.
XNU reaches VM, GIC, IOKit and framebuffer output on physical hardware.
UFS link recovery and read-only block device enumeration from XNU.
Real iOS HFS+ root mounts read-write and Apple launchd executes.
SpringBoard home screen is visible after synthetic unlock.
Physical touch unlocks iOS and operates Settings, Control Center and app navigation.
Probe reads power and both volume keys; no iOS key integration verified at this revision.

lessons.title: Transport success is not code execution
lessons.finding: fastboot boot replied OKAY after reporting its command was not implemented.
lessons.application: Require independent execution evidence (screen marker, kernel log or readback) before claiming RAM boot support.
lessons.caveat: Fastboot command sets and behaviour depend on bootloader and firmware.

lessons.title: Firmware-matched restore and live preflight
lessons.finding: OTA changed bootloader and slot state; matching stock images and AVB chain were verified before writes.
lessons.application: Record firmware fingerprint, current slot, pending snapshot merge, stock restore hash and rollback before any writable experiment.
lessons.caveat: The G54's boot_a write and Virtual A/B gates do not generalise to all phones; Nexus does not authorise writes.

lessons.title: Measure visible scanout, not advertised framebuffer
lessons.finding: LK's DT handoff framebuffer and visible overlay had different bases/strides; only scanout-register inspection exposed the visible buffer.
lessons.application: Instrument panel markers; read active overlay/RDMA or equivalent; verify width, pixel order, stride, cache visibility and reservation before setting XNU framebuffer.
lessons.caveat: Addresses, register layout and overlays are MT6855/LK-specific.

lessons.title: Verify exception level and kernel handoff explicitly
lessons.finding: LK entered at EL1, not the EL2 seen on related hardware; MMU granule, memory window, GIC and timer were measured.
lessons.application: Build tiny visible probes, inspect firmware DTB/boot args/PSCI and reserved RAM, then test one CPU before SMP and IOKit.
lessons.caveat: Do not copy a sibling SoC's memory map or CPU affinities.

lessons.title: Diagnose UFS link state before filesystem
lessons.finding: G54 LK left the UFS device held in reset; transport returned OCS failure before reinitialisation; a vendor-order reset/HCE/UIC/link/device-init sequence restored usable block reads.
lessons.application: Separate link failure, UIC errors, SCSI sense, LUN discovery, partition and root mount into checkpoints; inspect OEM teardown and platform Linux driver before changing XNU.
lessons.caveat: The exact SiP calls, UIC attributes and controller registers are not portable.

lessons.title: Storage link mode can dominate boot latency
lessons.finding: Link in PWM slow-auto took tens of minutes to reach the lock screen; changing to HS-G3 was followed by a reported 2-3 minute lock screen.
lessons.application: Record negotiated gear/lanes and errors; compare identical payload/root states where possible; tune link power mode only after basic read path works.
lessons.caveat: E20 combined console mute and HS mode, and writable root retained warm state; observed improvement is not a controlled causal estimate.

lessons.title: Validate host-created iOS root before mounting
lessons.finding: macOS builder required ownership-preserving mounts, HFS+ fsck and a sparse-image round trip before a successful userdata flash.
lessons.application: Check OS build/architecture, ownership, symlinks, shared-cache hardlinks, filesystem integrity and device capacity; hash raw/sparse reconstruction.
lessons.caveat: HFS+ and Android sparse are specific to this iOS 16 source-XNU route; writable roots invalidate old-image sparse-diff assumptions.

lessons.title: Milestones require distinct observables
lessons.finding: An XNU screen and later launchd/SpringBoard exec preceded real framebuffer UI and touch by distinct experiments.
lessons.application: Track kernel, storage, root, PID 1, framebuffer frames, home screen and physical input separately; never infer higher milestones from logs naming a process.
lessons.caveat: The source reports are owner observations; Nexus did not reproduce G54 hardware milestones.

lessons.title: Separate bus, flashless firmware, report format and HID
lessons.finding: Live DT overlay selected Novatek SPI3; chip ID, proprietary firmware boot, 4x big-endian reports/checksum, and XNU HID event delivery were each tested in succession.
lessons.application: Identify active panel and bus; prove chip reads; keep firmware local; decode reports against stock driver/docs and verify checksum/range; then map contacts to OS HID.
lessons.caveat: The Novatek protocol and G54 SPI3 pinmux must not become shared driver code; E26 used polled input, not IRQ.

lessons.title: Verify patch application and binary identity
lessons.finding: Pinned CI builds have explicit patchset and exec-data checks; build driver can silently skip failed patches.
lessons.application: Gate expected patch count/reverse-apply and executable-data signatures, retain exact compiler/runner/source pins; never promote build success to device boot.
lessons.caveat: Segment equality is not complete binary identity; boot verification remains separate.

lessons.title: Sample affected processes before changing patches
lessons.finding: SpringBoard dyld/ObjC and service waits progressed across repeated samples; unrelated workaround patches were not assumed needed.
lessons.application: Symbolicate against the exact shared cache; distinguish process restarts, page faults, stalls and daemon resource limits; change one causal variable per run where feasible.
lessons.caveat: dtrace_dof_mode=0 coincided with progress but no isolated causal performance proof exists.

lessons.title: PMIC key reads are not an iOS key driver
lessons.finding: All three keys were observed in the probe; repeated full resets correlated with button presses, not with key polling alone.
lessons.application: Use stock DT and PMIC/SPMI drivers for ownership/IRQ/long-press policy; test key handling with reset diagnostics before enabling in iOS.
lessons.caveat: Restart cause is unresolved and 0203 had no physical iOS validation at this source pin.

open_questions.question: Are physical-key resets caused by PMIC long-press configuration or an unserviced key interrupt?
open_questions.next_test: Observe one bounded key press and capture reset reason using the G54 project's approved recovery loop; test the 0203 driver separately.

open_questions.question: Do white docks/blur, blank widgets and tearing share a CPU framebuffer composition or synchronisation bug?
open_questions.next_test: Compare per-layer surface formats and alpha at fixed frames, then measure presentation and vsync before designing GPU work.

open_questions.question: Can this platform support reliable physical USB diagnostics, audio, networking and hardware graphics?
open_questions.next_test: Investigate one device subsystem at a time from stock DT/driver probes, then isolate transport/driver/userspace before claiming support.
